question.leadin: Eamon de Valera founded this nation's largest political party, Fianna Fail.
question.text: Name this nation, with capital at Dublin. Its northern neighbor is still part of the United Kingdom.
question.clue: Leaders from this country include Eamon de Valera and Patrick Pearse.

swap.text: During the crisis of the Third Century Aurelian built a set of these structures around Rome. Antonius Pius and Hadrian each built one of these structures that marked the northern border of the empire.
swap.answerHtml: walls [accept Aurelian Walls; accept Severan Walls; accept Hadrian’s Wall; accept Antonine Wall]
swap.clue: Palm oil lamps lit these objects in a huge system credited to Ewuare in Benin.

question.leadin: This organization agreed to disarm in the Good Friday Agreement, which ended a decades-long conflict known as The Troubles.
question.text: Name this paramilitary organization which conducted bombings and assassinations in Northern Ireland in the late 20th century.
question.answerHtml: IRA [or Irish Republican Army; or the Provisional Irish Republican Army]
question.clue: Anthony Berry was among the victims of the Brighton hotel bombing that was executed by this group during a failed attempt to assassinate Margaret Thatcher.

swap.leadin: This party's name means "Ours Alone" or "We Ourselves."
swap.text: Name this political party, which does not sit in the British Parliament, founded by Arthur Griffith. This Irish Republican political party was once led by Gerry Adams as well as former IRA leader Martin McGuinness.
swap.clue: Former Tanaiste Eamon Gilmore was originally a member of this party before eventually joining the Labour Party.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about Irish Home Rule.
question.text: Members of the Irish National Invincibles killed Irish Home Secretary Lord Cavendish and Thomas Burke in this 1882 set of stabbings that took place in Dublin.
question.clue: It resulted in the death of a man married to Prime Minister Gladstone's niece.

swap.text: This illuminated Irish manuscript was a compilation of parts of the Vulgate and the Vetus Latina. It is especially known for its illustrations.
swap.clue: A masterpiece of the Hiberno-Saxon style, this manuscript, begun in the late 8th century, was moved from the Isle of Iona to the monastery that gives it its name. It is also sometimes known as the Book of Columba.

question.text: This agreement, negotiated in 1998 with the help of Tony Blair, ended the Troubles by effectively dismantling the Provisional IRA.
question.clue: Bertie Ahern and David Andrews were signatories of this document, which was primarily negotiated by David Trimble and John Hume.

swap.leadin: "I ran away with two old people, but they were caught and killed, and the soldiers made me carry the baskets holding their cut-off hands."
swap.text: These horrors were described in a 1903 report by this Irish diplomat and activist. This man detailed systematic abuses being perpetrated in the Congo Free State.
swap.clue: This man's lawyer, A. M. Sullivan, tried to argue that there was a comma after the word "realm" in the clause "realm or elsewhere" in the 1351 statute this man was charged with violating; as a result, this man was said to have been "hanged on a comma."

question.text: In 1873, Parnell displaced the less militant Isaac Butt as leader of the "league" named for this phrase, which was the contemporary name for the goal of Irish autonomists.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a historical event.
swap.text: This former school teacher and barrister served as one of the commanders of the Easter Rising. He was declared President of the Provisional Government and executed after the British retook Dublin.
swap.clue: This man praised war for warming the "heart of the earth" with the "red wine of battlefields," a metaphor reflecting his mystical belief in "blood sacrifice."

question.text: In the 1918 "Coupon" election, Lloyd George retained his ministry in a coalition with the Conservatives under Andrew Bonar Law. In that election, the Sinn Fein party, led by this man, took 73 seats. This man founded the party Fianna Fail and was president of Ireland from 1959 to 1973.
question.clue: This leader's American citizenship allowed him to escape execution after the Easter Rising.

swap.text: This man also took part in the Easter Rebellion. As the IRA Director of Intelligence, he was a leader of the Irish War of Independence, and he signed the unpopular Anglo-Irish Treaty.
swap.clue: This leader of an assassination group known as The Squad was imprisoned at Frongoch internment camp for their role as aide-de-camp to Joseph Plunkett during the Easter Rising.

question.text: All six prime ministers of Northern Ireland belonged to this political party, which dominated Unionist politics after partition.
question.clue: With John Hume of the SDLP, this party's leader won the 1998 Nobel Peace Prize for facilitating the Good Friday Agreement.

swap.leadin: The speaker of this poem laments, "Too long a sacrifice / can make a stone of the heart."
swap.text: Name this poem in which William Butler Yeats memorializes "MacDonagh and MacBride / and Connolly and Pearse," who were killed as a result of an uprising.
swap.clue: This failed rebellion by Sinn Fein lead by Patrick Pearse and James Connolly to establish an independent Ireland that took place during the eponymous week.

question.text: The Boston tapes supposedly implicated this longtime leader of Sinn Fein in McConville's kidnapping, for which he was briefly arrested in 2014. This leader has long claimed, rather implausibly, that he was never a member of the IRA.
question.clue: In interviews for an oral history project conducted by Boston College, Brendan Hughes and Dolours Price implicated this person in the murder of Jean McConville.

swap.text: This younger sister of Charles Parnell led the Ladies' Land League and wrote The Tale of a Great Sham. A plaque on her tombstone carries her quote "the best part of independence; the independence of mind."
swap.answerHtml: Anna Catherine Parnell [grudgingly prompt on (A.) Parnell ]

question.text: This Irish lawyer founded the Home Government Association in 1870, which transformed into the Home Rule League later led by Parnell. He opposed O'Connell early on, and supported a feudal system for Ireland.

swap.leadin: This man became the first president of Michael Davitt's Irish Land League, and he negotiated the Kilmainham Treaty with the government of William Gladstone.
swap.text: Name this Irish advocate of Home Rule, who was erroneously linked to the Phoenix Park murders.
swap.clue: He also gained status due to the deaths of T.H. Burke and Frederick Cavendish in , which allowed him to displace the National League with his own Home Rule Party.

question.leadin: The head of the last Catholic martyr in English history is preserved in this city, which was conquered by the Parliamentarians in 1649.
question.text: Name this Irish seaport where a notorious massacre took place.
question.clue: Over a thousand survivors of the initial breach of the walls here were caught and killed in St. Peter's Church.

swap.leadin: This politician conspired with Lord Russell's Whigs to try and unseat Robert Peel in exchange for some reforms via the Lichfield House Compact.
swap.text: Name this man. Parliament refused to seat him after his election to the MPship in County Clare, Ireland, until this man's agitations got the Catholic Emancipation Act passed.
swap.clue: Among this man's political projects were the signing of the Lichfield House Compact to form an unlikely political alliance and the organization of "monster meetings" such as the one at Tara on behalf of the Repeal Association.
